questions.question: If a man deposits Rs. 12,100 in a bank at a simple interest of 15% per annum, then how much money will he receive from the bank after 3 years?
questions.questionHtml: If a man deposits Rs. 12,100 in a bank at a simple interest of 15% per annum, then how much money will he receive from the bank after 3 years?
questions.solution:
Given:
Type = Simple
Principle = Rs. 12,100
Rate = 15%
Time = 3 years

Formula used:
SI = (P x R x T) /100

A = SI + P
here, 
A = Amount
SI = Simple Interest
P = Principle
R = Rate
T = Time

Solution:
Let's put the values given, in the formula to find the value of SI;

SI = (12100 x 15 x 3) /100 = 5445

Now,

A = 12100 + 5445 = 17545

Hence, he will get Rs. 17,545 at the end of 3rd year.

questions.question: A certain sum becomes Rs. 1,050 in 5 years and Rs. 1,230 in 8 years at simple interest. What is the sum?
questions.questionHtml: A certain sum becomes Rs. 1,050 in 5 years and Rs. 1,230 in 8 years at simple interest. What is the sum?
questions.solution:
Calculation:

Let the sum be P and the rate of interest be r

Simple interest = PRT/100

⇒ 1050 = P + PR × (5/100)

⇒ P(1 + 5R/100) = 1050        -------(1)

⇒ 1230 = P + PR × (8/100)

⇒ P(1 + 8R/100) = 1230        -------(2)

Solving (1) and (2), 

⇒ (1 + 5R/100)/(1 + 8R/100) = 1050/1230

⇒ (1 + 5R/100)/(1 + 8R/100) = 35/41

⇒ 41(1 + 5R/100) = 35(1 + 8R/100)

⇒ 41 + 205R/100 = 35 + 280R/100

⇒ 75R/100 = 6

⇒ R = 6 × 4/3

⇒ R = 8%

Put the value in (1)

⇒ P(1 + 5 × 8/100) = 1050 

⇒ P = 1050 × 5/7

⇒ P = Rs. 750

∴ Option 4 is the correct answer.

Where, P = Principal, t = Time (in years), r = rate of interest

questions.question: What will be the difference between the interest on a sum of Rs. 2,000 at 7% per annum for 3 years and that on a sum of Rs. 3,200 at 6% per annum for 2 years?
questions.questionHtml: What will be the difference between the interest on a sum of Rs. 2,000 at 7% per annum for 3 years and that on a sum of Rs. 3,200 at 6% per annum for 2 years?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Net Simple Interest percentage for Case 1 = 7% × 3 = 21%

Interest 1 (SI1) = 21% of ₹2,000 = ₹420

Net Simple Interest percentage for Case 2 = 6% × 2 = 12%

Interest 2 (SI2) = 12% of ₹3,200 = ₹384

Required Difference = 420 − 384 = ₹36

∴ The correct answer is ₹36.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal1 (P1) = ₹2,000, Rate1 (R1) = 7%, Time1 (T1) = 3 years

Principal2 (P2) = ₹3,200, Rate2 (R2) = 6%, Time2 (T2) = 2 years

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Calculations:

⇒ SI1 = (2000 × 7 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ SI1 = 20 × 21 = ₹420

⇒ SI2 = (3200 × 6 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI2 = 32 × 12 = ₹384

⇒ Difference = SI1 − SI2

⇒ Difference = 420 − 384 = ₹36

∴ The correct answer is ₹36.

Additional Information

Simple Interest (SI)

The interest calculated only on the initial principal amount for the entire duration. Formula: SI = (P × R × T)/100.

Total Amount (A)

The total sum of money returned after the time period, which includes the principal and the interest. A = P + SI.

Effective Rate of Interest

For Simple Interest, the effective rate for the entire period is simply the product of the annual rate and time (R × T)%.

Difference between SI and CI

For a 2-year period, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest is given by: D = P(R/100)2.

questions.question: The difference of simple interest on a sum of money for 8 years and 10 years is ₹ 200. If the rate of interest is 10 % p.a, then what is the sum of money?
questions.questionHtml: The difference of simple interest on a sum of money for 8 years and 10 years is ₹ 200. If the rate of interest is 10 % p.a, then what is the sum of money?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Difference in Time = 10 years − 8 years = 2 years.

Effective Interest Rate difference = 2 years × 10% = 20%.

Given that 20% of the Principal (Sum) = ₹ 200.

Sum (100%) = (200 ÷ 20) × 100 = ₹ 1,000.

∴ The correct answer is ₹ 1,000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Difference in Simple Interest (SI) = ₹ 200

Rate of Interest (R) = 10% p.a.

Time periods: T1 = 8 years and T2 = 10 years

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Calculations:

⇒ SI10 − SI8 = 200

⇒ [(P × 10 × 10) ÷ 100] − [(P × 10 × 8) ÷ 100] = 200

⇒ (100P ÷ 100) − (80P ÷ 100) = 200

⇒ P − 0.8P = 200

⇒ 0.2P = 200

⇒ P = 200 ÷ 0.2

⇒ P = 1000

∴ The correct answer is ₹ 1,000.

Additional Information

Simple Interest Difference Rule

When the principal and rate are constant, the difference in interest is directly proportional to the difference in time: SIdiff = P × R × (T2 − T1) ÷ 100.

Total Amount Formula

The total amount (A) after T years is the sum of Principal (P) and Simple Interest (SI): A = P + (P × R × T ÷ 100) = P(1 + RT ÷ 100).

Effective Rate of Interest

The effective interest for a period is the product of the annual rate and the number of years (R × T) expressed as a percentage of the principal.

questions.question: The sum of simple interest on a sum at 8% p.a. for 4 years and 8 years is Rs. 960. The sum is:

SI for 8 years = (a × 8 × 8)/100

⇒ 64a/100

⇒ (32a/100) + (64a/100) = 960

⇒ 96a/100 = 960

⇒ a = (960 × 100)/96

⇒ a = Rs. 1000

∴ The sum is Rs. 1000.

questions.question: A person lent Rs. 12,000 to B for 3 years and Rs. 10,000 to C for 4 years on simple interest at the same rate of interest and received Rs. 6,080 in all from both of them as interest. What is the annual rate of interest?
questions.questionHtml: A person lent Rs. 12,000 to B for 3 years and Rs. 10,000 to C for 4 years on simple interest at the same rate of interest and received Rs. 6,080 in all from both of them as interest. What is the annual rate of interest?
questions.solution:
Given:

Principal amount lent to B = Rs. 12,000

Time period for B = 3 years

Principal amount lent to C = Rs. 10,000

Time period for C = 4 years

Total interest received = Rs. 6,080

Formula used:

Simple interest = (Principal amount × Time period × Rate of interest)/100

Solution:

The total interest received is the sum of the interest received from B and the interest received from C.

Interest received from B = (12,000 × 3 × R)/100

Interest received from C = (10,000 × 4 × R)/100

6,080 = (12,000 × 3 × R)/100 + (10,000 × 4 × R)/100

6,080 = 360R + 400R

6,080 = 760R

R = 6,080 / 760

R = 8%

Therefore, the annual rate of interest is 8%.

questions.question: The difference between simple interest on a certain sum at the annual rate of 8 percent for 5 years and 6 years is Rs. 26. What is the sum?
questions.questionHtml: The difference between simple interest on a certain sum at the annual rate of 8 percent for 5 years and 6 years is Rs. 26. What is the sum?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Difference in Time = 6 years − 5 years = 1 year.

Difference in Simple Interest percentage = 8% × 1 = 8%.

Given that 8% of the Sum = Rs. 26.

Total Sum (100%) = (26 ÷ 8) × 100 = 3.25 × 100 = 325.

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 325.

Alternate Method

Given:

Rate (R) = 8% per annum, Time1 (T1) = 5 years, Time2 (T2) = 6 years.

Difference between Simple Interests = Rs. 26.

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Calculations:

⇒ Let the Sum (Principal) be P.

⇒ SI for 6 years = (P × 8 × 6) ÷ 100 = 48P ÷ 100

⇒ SI for 5 years = (P × 8 × 5) ÷ 100 = 40P ÷ 100

⇒ Difference = (48P ÷ 100) − (40P ÷ 100) = 26

⇒ 8P ÷ 100 = 26

⇒ 8P = 2600

⇒ P = 2600 ÷ 8

⇒ P = 325

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 325.

Additional Information

Relationship between SI and Time

For a constant Principal and Rate, the Simple Interest is directly proportional to the Time period (SI ∝ T). Thus, SI2 − SI1 = P × R × (T2 − T1) ÷ 100.

Calculation of Total Amount

The Total Amount (A) after any period is the sum of the Principal and the Interest earned: A = P + SI = P × (1 + RT ÷ 100).

Finding Rate or Time

If the Principal and Interest are known, the Rate (R) can be found using R = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T) and Time (T) using T = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × R).

⇒ Simple Interest = 100

Simple Interest = (P × r × t)/100

⇒ 100 = (100 × r × 12)/100

⇒ r = 100/12

⇒ r = 25/3

\( \Rightarrow {\rm{r}} = 8\frac{1}{3}\;\% \)

∴ The rate of interest is \(8\frac{1}{3}\;\% .\)

questions.question: How much simple interest will ₹5,000 earn in 14 months at a 12% interest rate per annum?
questions.questionHtml: How much simple interest will ₹5,000 earn in 14 months at a 12% interest rate per annum?
questions.solution:
Given:

Principal (P) = ₹5,000

Time (T) = 14 months = 14/12 years = 7/6 years

Rate of interest (R) = 12% per annum

Formula used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

Calculation:

SI = (₹5,000 × 12 × 7/6) / 100

⇒ SI = (₹5,000 × 12 × 7) / (6 × 100)

⇒ SI = (₹5,000 × 2 × 7) / 100

⇒ SI = (₹5,000 × 14) / 100

⇒ SI = ₹70,000 / 100

⇒ SI = ₹700

∴ The simple interest earned is ₹700.

questions.question: A sum at a simple interest of 8% p.a. becomes 7/5 of itself in how many years?
questions.questionHtml: A sum at a simple interest of 8% p.a. becomes 7/5 of itself in how many years?
questions.solution:
Let the sum be P and time be T.

Interest earn on the sum = (7/5) P – P = (2/5) P

Rate of interest = R = 8 %

Simple Interest = PRT / 100

(2/5)P = P × 8 × T /100

⇒ T = 5 years

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 3000 becomes Rs. 6000 when invested in a scheme of simple interest. If the annual rate of interest and the number of years for which the sum was invested are same, then what is the annual rate of interest?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of Rs. 3000 becomes Rs. 6000 when invested in a scheme of simple interest. If the annual rate of interest and the number of years for which the sum was invested are same, then what is the annual rate of interest?
questions.solution:
Given:

Principal = Rs. 3000

Amount = Rs. 6000

Concept Used: 

Simple Interest = PRT/100

Simple Interest = Amount - Principal

Calculation:

Let the rate of interest be r% and as the time is equal to rate of interest.

So, time = r years

Simple Interest = Amount - Principal

Simple Interest = 6000 - 3000 = Rs. 3000

Simple Interest = PRT/100

3000 = 3000 × r × r/100

r2 = 100

r = 10

Annual rate of interest = 10%

∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question: In a certain duration of time, a sum become 2 times itself at the rate of 5% per annum simple interest. What will be the rate of interest if the same sum becomes 5 times itself in the same duration?
questions.questionHtml: In a certain duration of time, a sum become 2 times itself at the rate of 5% per annum simple interest. What will be the rate of interest if the same sum becomes 5 times itself in the same duration?
questions.solution:
According to question, P × 5 × T/100 = P ⇒ T = 20 years

Now, P × R × T/100 = 4P ⇒ P × R × 20/100 = 4P ⇒ R = 4 × 5 = 20%

questions.question: What would be the simple interest (in ₹) on principal amount of ₹ 1 lakh for 2 years at the rate of 12 percent per annum?
questions.questionHtml: What would be the simple interest (in ₹) on principal amount of ₹ 1 lakh for 2 years at the rate of 12 percent per annum?
questions.solution:
Given:

The sum = Rs. 1 lakh

The rate of interest = 12%

Time = 2 years

Formula used:

\(S.I.={P× R× T\over100}\)     Where, S.I.  = Simple interest, P = Principle, R = Rate, and T

Calculation:

Let the simple interest is X

⇒ X = \({100000× 12 × 2\over100}\)

⇒ X = 1000 × 12 × 2 = 24000

∴ The required result will be 24000.

questions.question: An amount of Rs. 50,000 becomes Rs. 72,000 in 4 years on a simple rate of interest. The rate of interest is _____ per annum.
questions.questionHtml: An amount of Rs. 50,000 becomes Rs. 72,000 in 4 years on a simple rate of interest. The rate of interest is _____ per annum.
questions.solution:
P = Rs. 50,000, A = Rs. 72,000, T = 4 years

SI = A - P = 72,000 - 50,000 = Rs. 22,000

R = (SI × 100) / (P × T) = (22,000 × 100) / (50,000 × 4) = 11%

questions.question: When two equal amounts are deposited for 5 years and 3 years at a rate of 7% and 9% per annum respectively, and the difference of their simple interest is Rs. 475. Then find the deposited amount.
questions.questionHtml: When two equal amounts are deposited for 5 years and 3 years at a rate of 7% and 9% per annum respectively, and the difference of their simple interest is Rs. 475. Then find the deposited amount.
questions.solution:
Let sum be Rs. x

As we know,

SI = Prt/100

According to the question

(x × 5 × 7)/100 – (x × 3 × 9)/100 = 475

⇒ (35x – 27x)/100 = 475

⇒ 8x/100 = 475

⇒ x = 475 × (100/8)

⇒ x = 5937.5

Short Trick:

Let the sum be 100%

According to the question

⇒ 35% - 27% = 475

⇒ 8% = 475

⇒ 100% = 475/8 × 100 = 5937.5

questions.question: Money was lent on simple interest. After 12 years, its simple interest becomes \(\frac{3}{5}\) of the money. Find the rate of interest.
questions.questionHtml: Money was lent on simple interest. After 12 years, its simple interest becomes \(\frac{3}{5}\) of the money. Find the rate of interest.
questions.solution:
Total Simple Interest percentage = (3 ÷ 5) × 100 = 60%

We know directly that Total SI% = Rate × Time

60% = Rate × 12

Rate = 60 ÷ 12 = 5%

questions.question: An amount will be triple itself in 15 years at a certain rate of simple interest per annum. The rate of interest per annum is:
questions.questionHtml: An amount will be triple itself in 15 years at a certain rate of simple interest per annum. The rate of interest per annum is:
questions.solution:
Let the principal amount be P

Total Amount (A) = 3P, SI = 2P, Using SI = P × R × T / 100,

2P = P × R × 15 / 100 ⇒ 2 = 15R / 100 ⇒ R = 200 / 15 = \(13\frac{1}{3}\) %

questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum of money at the rate of 8% p.a. for 9 years is ₹2,880. At what rate of interest can the same amount of interest can be received on the same sum for 12 years?
questions.questionHtml: The simple interest on a certain sum of money at the rate of 8% p.a. for 9 years is ₹2,880. At what rate of interest can the same amount of interest can be received on the same sum for 12 years?
questions.solution:
Given:

Simple Interest = Rs. 2880

Rate % = 8% p.a

Time = 9 years

Formula used:

Simple Interest = PTR/100 

Where,

P = principal

R = rate %

T = time

Calculation:

Let the principal be P

According to the concept,

2880 = (P × 8 × 9)/100

⇒ 2880 = (72P)/100

⇒ P = 2880 × 100/72

⇒ P = Rs. 4000

Let rate for 12 years for same interest to be found be R 

2880 = (4000 × 12 × R)/100

⇒ 2880 = 48000R/100 

⇒ R = 2880 × 100/48000

⇒ R = 6%

∴ The required rate percent is 6%

questions.question: The simple interest on a sum of money in 6 years at the rate of 15% per annum is Rs. 1,440 less than the simple interest accrued on the same sum in 9 years at 18% per annum. What is the sum of money (in Rs.)?
questions.questionHtml: The simple interest on a sum of money in 6 years at the rate of 15% per annum is Rs. 1,440 less than the simple interest accrued on the same sum in 9 years at 18% per annum. What is the sum of money (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
Let the principal be P.

1440 = [(P × 18 × 9)/100] - [(P × 15 × 6)/100]  ⇒ 1440 = 162P/100 - 90P/100 ⇒ 1440 = 72P/100 ⇒ P = 2000

questions.question: The simple interest received on a sum is 25/36 of the sum. The number of years is equal to the annual rate of interest. What is the annual rate of interest?
questions.questionHtml: The simple interest received on a sum is 25/36 of the sum. The number of years is equal to the annual rate of interest. What is the annual rate of interest?
questions.solution:
SI = (x × R × T)/100

⇒ (25/36)x = (x × R2)/100 ⇒ 25/36 = R2/100

Taking square-root both sides, we get

⇒ 5/6 = R/10 ⇒ R = 0.833 × 10 = 8.33%

questions.question: The interest on a certain deposit at 4.5% p.a. is ₹135 in one year. How much will the additional interest in one year be on the same deposit at 5% p.a.?
questions.questionHtml: The interest on a certain deposit at 4.5% p.a. is ₹135 in one year. How much will the additional interest in one year be on the same deposit at 5% p.a.?
questions.solution:
Let deposit = Rs. a 

⇒ 135 = (a x 4.5 x 1)/100 ⇒ a = 3000

Simple interest on 5% = (3000 x 5 x 1)/100 ⇒ 150

Additional interest = 150 - 135 = Rs. 15

questions.question: In how much time will ₹5,000 at 4% per annum simple interest produce the same interest as ₹8,000 in \(2\frac{1}{2}\) years at 8% per annum simple interest?
questions.questionHtml: In how much time will ₹5,000 at 4% per annum simple interest produce the same interest as ₹8,000 in \(2\frac{1}{2}\) years at 8% per annum simple interest?
questions.solution:
SI = (P × r × t)/100

Interest from ₹8,000 = (8000 × 8 × 5)/(2 × 100) = ₹1,600

Principal (P1) = ₹5,000, Rate (r1) = 4%

SI = (5000 × 4 × t1)/100, 200 × t1 = 1600 

t1 = 1600/200 = 8 years
